mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6.0% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, reducing corporate margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE < 6.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive monthly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month MA +2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods when INDPRO exceeds its 12-month MA by >2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous two-month decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and new home sales (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in household demand, which depresses corporate revenue and profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising at an annualized rate above 2.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a low-rate, high-inflation environment that erodes real yields and compresses equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL y/y inflation > 2.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods meeting the FEDFUNDS/CPIAUCSL trigger.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the monthly change in industrial production (INDPRO) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days; a month-over-month increase in INDPRO of at least 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns within the following week.
failure_condition: The conditional probability of a positive S&P 500 5-day return given INDPRO > 0.5% monthly change is not significantly above 50% (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
